name: Barnard's Star
blurb: The star with the fastest apparent motion in the sky: over 10 arcseconds a year, almost due north.
discovery_ref: Brief target; discovery reference not looked up. Not a Backyard Worlds discovery.
notes: Saturates SPHEREx in every detector (OVERFLOW/SUR_ERROR/BLOOM). Motion demo only. Saturated in AllWISE too (W1/W2 flagged).
photometry_source: AllWISE J175747.94+044323.8 (epoch about 2010.5; ph_qual BBAA, cc_flags hHH0)

name: Epsilon Indi Ba/Bb
blurb: Two brown dwarfs (T1 and T6) orbiting each other, 12 light years from the Sun.
known_type_ref: Chen et al. 2022, arXiv:2205.08077 (abstract opened); SIMBAD lists T1V+T6V, bibcode 2005AJ....129.2849B
discovery_ref: Brief target; discovery reference not looked up. Not a Backyard Worlds discovery.
notes: Best SPHEREx spectrum demo: 106/107 frames clean, CH4, CO2 and CO visible. Gaia RUWE 4.3 (unresolved pair), astrometry approximate. CatWISE2020 fits it badly (pm about 1.1 arcsec/yr against 4.7 true), so Gaia is adopted.

pm_second_reference.source: Chen et al. 2022, AJ 163, 288, arXiv:2205.08077, Table 4 (the Ba+Bb pair with its orbit modelled; frame tied to Gaia EDR3)
pm_second_reference.caveat: That match is expected only if the two brown dwarfs share the light at 4.6 um roughly as they share the mass, which has not been measured. This second reference was added after the mismatch with Gaia DR3 was seen; the row is still scored against Gaia DR3.
pm_second_reference.added: 2026-11-15, after the motion check against Gaia DR3 had failed

photometry_source: AllWISE J220415.75-564724.4 (epoch about 2010.5; ph_qual AAAB, cc_flags hh00)

name: WISE 0855-0714
blurb: One of the coldest brown dwarfs known, 7.4 light years away and moving more than 8 arcseconds a year.
known_type_ref: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021, ApJS 253, 7, arXiv:2011.11616, doi:10.3847/1538-4365/abd107, Table A1 adopted type 24.0; no near-IR spectral type exists (SIMBAD lists Y2, bibcode 2015ApJ...799...37L)
discovery_ref: Brief target; discovery reference not looked up. Not a Backyard Worlds discovery.
notes: Detected by SPHEREx at 3.8-5 um (S/N about 11 stacked) and moves as predicted, but too faint for a spectrum with molecular bands. The brief's coordinate (RA 133.7951, Dec -7.2451) is the WISE-designation position at about 2010.5, not 2015. Live CatWISE2020 splits it into fragments (W2 15.7-15.8); the W2 here is the K21 value, backed by Spitzer ch2 13.92.
position_source: CatWISE2020 J085507.96-071439.3 motion-fit position (ra_pm, dec_pm), MJD 57170 = 2015.405
pm_source: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021 Table A1 (parallax programme; astrometry code AT)
photometry_source: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021 Table A1 (CatWISE2020 W1/W2 as tabulated there)

name: RW Aurigae A
blurb: A young multiple-star system in Auriga, about 510 light years away.
known_type_ref: K1/5e+K5e, SIMBAD bibcode 1999A&A...351..954D (paper not opened); SIMBAD lists K6 for the Gaia source (2021ApJS..254...20L)
discovery_ref: Brief target; discovery reference not looked up.
notes: Brighter of two Gaia sources 1.5 arcsec apart (G 12.18), so blended in SPHEREx and WISE. Saturates SPHEREx (65 of 109 frames masked, spherex-data.md). Saturated in AllWISE.
photometry_source: AllWISE J050749.54+302404.7 (epoch about 2010.5; ph_qual AAAA, cc_flags 0000)

name: R Draconis
blurb: A pulsating red giant (a Mira variable) in Draco, roughly 2,600 light years away, that brightens and fades over months.
known_type_ref: M4.5-6+e, SIMBAD bibcode 1966ApJS...13..333K (paper not opened); type varies with phase
discovery_ref: Brief target; discovery reference not looked up.
notes: Saturates every SPHEREx detector, so no spectrum or light curve from L2 pixels. W1/W2 are saturated in AllWISE and the values are lower limits on brightness. Only source brighter than G 12 within 36 arcsec.
photometry_source: AllWISE J163240.19+664517.9 (epoch about 2010.5; ph_qual UUAA, cc_flags hh00)

name: WISEA J1101+5400
blurb: The first brown dwarf found by Backyard Worlds volunteers, a T dwarf about 110 light years away.
known_type_ref: Kuchner et al. 2017, ApJL 841, L19, arXiv:1705.02919, doi:10.3847/2041-8213/aa7200 (IRTF/SpeX prism spectrum, Gk fit)
discovery_ref: Kuchner et al. 2017, arXiv:1705.02919. Flagged by several volunteers within a week of the 15 Feb 2017 launch; the paper does not name them.
notes: Marginal for SPHEREx: W2 15.37 in the paper (15.58 in live CatWISE2020), at the faint end of the rule. Expect WISE blink and motion, not a spectrum.
position_source: CatWISE2020 J110125.55+540053.4 motion-fit position (ra_pm, dec_pm), MJD 57170 = 2015.405

name: CWISE J0623+0715
blurb: A cool T dwarf low in heavy elements (a subdwarf), flagged by Backyard Worlds and moving 1 arcsecond a year.
discovery_ref: Burgasser et al. 2024, arXiv:2411.01378; candidate selected from Backyard Worlds: Planet 9 flipbooks. Zooniverse volunteers of Backyard Worlds: Planet 9, thanked collectively; the paper names no individual discoverer.
notes: W2 15.0: motion and detection demo; a SPHEREx spectrum is unlikely. Metal-poor, so a good test of whether the template match fails gracefully.
position_source: CatWISE2020 J062316.19+071505.6 motion-fit position (ra_pm, dec_pm), MJD 57170 = 2015.405
pm_source: Burgasser et al. 2024, arXiv:2411.01378, Table 9 (Sample Kinematics; errors 32 and 37 mas/yr; reference [7], their own measurement). Table 11, cited before by mistake, is T Subdwarf Spectral Standards

name: CWISE J2112-0529
blurb: A cool T subdwarf found through Backyard Worlds, moving 0.9 arcseconds a year.
discovery_ref: Burgasser et al. 2024, arXiv:2411.01378; abstract names it among three new metal-poor T subdwarfs from the Backyard Worlds programme. Zooniverse volunteers of Backyard Worlds: Planet 9, thanked collectively; the paper names no individual discoverer.
notes: Marginal: W2 15.35, near the faint limit of the rule. Live CatWISE2020 also lists a second fragment 2 arcsec away (W2 17.25). Motion demo only.
position_source: CatWISE2020 J211250.11-052925.2 motion-fit position (ra_pm, dec_pm), MJD 57170 = 2015.405
pm_source: Burgasser et al. 2024, arXiv:2411.01378, Table 9 (Sample Kinematics; errors 24 and 25 mas/yr; reference [7], their own measurement). Table 11, cited before by mistake, is T Subdwarf Spectral Standards

name: CWISE J2021+1524
blurb: A faint, metal-poor L dwarf found through Backyard Worlds, moving 0.7 arcseconds a year.
discovery_ref: Burgasser et al. 2024, arXiv:2411.01378; candidate from the Backyard Worlds search. Zooniverse volunteers of Backyard Worlds: Planet 9, thanked collectively; the paper names no individual discoverer.
notes: W2 14.7. CatWISE W1 carries a diffraction-spike flag (ab_flags D), so W1 is less reliable. Motion and detection demo.
position_source: CatWISE2020 J202130.08+152418.0 motion-fit position (ra_pm, dec_pm), MJD 57170 = 2015.405
pm_source: Burgasser et al. 2024, arXiv:2411.01378, Table 9 (Sample Kinematics; errors 3 and 3 mas/yr; reference [7], their own measurement). Table 11, cited before by mistake, is T Subdwarf Spectral Standards

name: CWISE J0411+4714
blurb: A late T dwarf with slightly low metal content, found through Backyard Worlds.
known_type_ref: Burgasser et al. 2024, arXiv:2411.01378 (Keck/NIRES spectrum); K21 Table A1 lists type 17.0 (T7) from photometry
discovery_ref: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021, ApJS 253, 7, arXiv:2011.11616, doi:10.3847/1538-4365/abd107, Table 1 discoverer codes A, D, N, R, W = Nikolaj Stevnbak Andersen, Dan Caselden, Kareem Ammar, Austin Rothermich, Jim Walla (legend in the paper's table notes; the paper does not say which of them first spotted it); spectrum and type from Burgasser et al. 2024, arXiv:2411.01378.
notes: W2 14.7, methane-rich so brighter at 4.5 um than in W1. Detection and motion demo; spectrum unlikely.
position_source: CatWISE2020 J041102.41+471422.6 motion-fit position (ra_pm, dec_pm), MJD 57170 = 2015.405
pm_source: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021 Table A1 (code Ac, equal to CatWISE2020)

name: CWISE J2029-7910
blurb: A blue L1 dwarf found by volunteers as a wide companion to an M6 star.
known_type_ref: Rothermich et al. 2024, arXiv:2403.04592 (SOAR/TripleSpec4 spectrum, 23 Oct 2021)
discovery_ref: Rothermich et al. 2024, arXiv:2403.04592; co-moving companion flagged by Backyard Worlds volunteers. Zooniverse volunteers of Backyard Worlds: Planet 9, thanked collectively; the paper names no individual discoverer.
notes: Right at the motion limit: 0.30 arcsec/yr. Host SCR J2029-7910 (M6, W2 about 11.1) is 34 arcsec away, 5.5 SPHEREx pixels.
sources: https://irsa.ipac.caltech.edu/TAP/sync (catwise_2020, cone at the 2015.405 position, fetched 2026-11-14)

name: CWISE J1055+5443
blurb: A nearby Y0 dwarf with unusual colours, about 22 light years away and moving 1.5 arcseconds a year.
known_type_ref: Robbins et al. 2023, arXiv:2310.09524 (Keck/NIRES spectrum); K21 Table A1 lists sdT8 from photometry
discovery_ref: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021, ApJS 253, 7, arXiv:2011.11616, doi:10.3847/1538-4365/abd107, Table 1 discoverer codes D, G, J = Dan Caselden, Samuel J. Goodman, J. Davy Kirkpatrick (legend in the paper's table notes); K21 gives Goodman a Backyard Worlds: Planet 9 affiliation. Robbins et al. 2023 lists the Backyard Worlds collaboration as authors but does not describe the discovery.
notes: W2 14.4 (K21; live CatWISE2020 fragments say 15.3-15.5): detection and motion demo, and a second Y dwarf next to WISE 0855. Discovery credit rests on the K21 Table 1 codes, not on a statement that a volunteer first spotted it.
position_source: CatWISE2020 J105512.11+544328.3 motion-fit position (ra_pm, dec_pm), MJD 57170 = 2015.405
pm_source: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021 Table A1 (parallax programme; astrometry code AT)
photometry_source: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021 Table A1 (CatWISE2020 W1/W2 as tabulated there)

name: DENIS J0255-4700
blurb: A nearby L9 brown dwarf, 16 light years away, moving 1.15 arcseconds a year.
known_type_ref: K21 Table A1 adopted L9 (optical L8, near-IR L9) Kirkpatrick et al. 2021, ApJS 253, 7, arXiv:2011.11616, doi:10.3847/1538-4365/abd107; SIMBAD L9, bibcode 2014AJ....147...34S
discovery_ref: Named for the DENIS survey; discovery paper not looked up. Benchmark, not a Backyard Worlds discovery.
notes: Brightest L/T-transition benchmark here (W2 10.2, Ks 11.6), so a SPHEREx spectrum is plausible (untested; Eps Ind B at Ks 11.2 was clean).
photometry_source: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021 Table A1 (CatWISE2020 W1/W2 as tabulated there)

name: 2MASS J0559-1404
blurb: A mid-T (T4.5) brown dwarf 34 light years away, moving 0.66 arcseconds a year.
known_type_ref: SIMBAD, bibcode 2002ApJ...564..466G; K21 Table A1 adopted T4.5 Kirkpatrick et al. 2021, ApJS 253, 7, arXiv:2011.11616, doi:10.3847/1538-4365/abd107
discovery_ref: Named for the 2MASS survey; discovery paper not looked up. Benchmark, not a Backyard Worlds discovery.
notes: Ks 13.6, W2 about 12: strongest at 4.5 um, so expect a detection with a usable red half of the spectrum (untested).
photometry_source: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021 Table A1 (CatWISE2020 W1/W2 as tabulated there)

name: 2MASS J0415-0935
blurb: A T8 brown dwarf 19 light years away with deep methane absorption, moving 2.3 arcseconds a year.
known_type_ref: SIMBAD, bibcode 2002ApJ...564..421B; K21 Table A1 adopted T8 Kirkpatrick et al. 2021, ApJS 253, 7, arXiv:2011.11616, doi:10.3847/1538-4365/abd107
discovery_ref: Named for the 2MASS survey; discovery paper not looked up. Benchmark, not a Backyard Worlds discovery.
notes: K 15.4: faint at SPHEREx's short wavelengths, so only the 3-5 um methane and CO2 region is likely usable (untested). Live CatWISE2020 splits it into two fragments; the one whose motion matches the literature is adopted, the other has pm 26% too high.
position_source: CatWISE2020 J041522.17-093457.1 motion-fit position (ra_pm, dec_pm), MJD 57170 = 2015.405
pm_source: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021 Table A1 (parallax programme; astrometry code AD)
photometry_source: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021 Table A1 (CatWISE2020 W1/W2 as tabulated there)

name: UGPS J0722-0540
blurb: One of the coolest T dwarfs (T9), 13 light years away, moving 1 arcsecond a year.
known_type_ref: SIMBAD, bibcode 2010MNRAS.408L..56L; K21 Table A1 adopted T9 Kirkpatrick et al. 2021, ApJS 253, 7, arXiv:2011.11616, doi:10.3847/1538-4365/abd107
discovery_ref: Named for the UKIDSS GPS; bibcode 2010MNRAS.408L..56L is SIMBAD's type reference (not opened). Benchmark, not a Backyard Worlds discovery.
notes: K 17, W2 12.2: a 4.5 um detection is likely, but the short-wavelength half of the spectrum will be empty (untested). Live CatWISE2020 has a second, fainter fragment 0.9 arcsec away.
position_source: CatWISE2020 J072226.89-054027.5 motion-fit position (ra_pm, dec_pm), MJD 57170 = 2015.405
pm_source: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021 Table A1 (parallax programme; astrometry code Al)
photometry_source: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021 Table A1 (CatWISE2020 W1/W2 as tabulated there)

name: WISE 1541-2250
blurb: A Y dwarf about 20 light years away, much cooler than a T dwarf, moving 0.9 arcseconds a year.
known_type_ref: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021, ApJS 253, 7, arXiv:2011.11616, doi:10.3847/1538-4365/abd107, Table A1 near-IR and adopted type 21.0 = Y1 (VizieR J/ApJS/253/7/tablea1, PName 1541-2250, read 2026-11-15); SIMBAD still lists Y0, bibcode 2011ApJS..197...19K (the discovery-era type)
discovery_ref: WISE discovery (name); bibcode 2011ApJS..197...19K is SIMBAD's type reference (not opened). Benchmark, not a Backyard Worlds discovery.
notes: W2 14.2: a detection-and-motion target for SPHEREx, like WISE 0855, not a spectrum target. Live CatWISE2020 gives W2 15.1 and 14.8 for two fragments.
position_source: CatWISE2020 J154151.41-225026.1 motion-fit position (ra_pm, dec_pm), MJD 57170 = 2015.405
pm_source: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021 Table A1 (parallax programme; astrometry code AT)
photometry_source: Kirkpatrick et al. 2021 Table A1 (CatWISE2020 W1/W2 as tabulated there)
